latest_release.name: v0.6.0
latest_release.body:
xquad 0.6 hardens the bytecode checker that decides whether a program may run: its analyses are bounded, so no program can make it hang or do more work than its size allows, and it now checks stack heights, registers and jumps exactly. It also fixes two VM issues raised in a security review, and `pip install xquad` becomes the one way to install the Python toolchain. The [migration guide from 0.5](https://developers.quip.network/docs/xquad/appendix/migration-0.6) covers every breaking change.

### Breaking changes

- **One Python distribution.** `xquad` now carries `xqffi`, `xqcp`, `xqsa` and the `xquad` CLI in one wheel; those three have no 0.6 release. Replace `pip install xqsa` (or `xqcp`, `xqffi`) with `pip install xquad`, and `xqsa[cuda]` with `xquad[cuda]`. Imports are unchanged. In an environment upgraded in place, run `pip uninstall -y xqffi xqcp xqsa`, then `pip install --force-reinstall xquad`; `import xquad` refuses to run next to the 0.5 distributions until you do.
- **Verifier renamed to checker.** `xqvm::verifier::verify` → `xqvm::checker::check`, `Verifier` → `Checker`, `VerifierError` → `CheckerError`, `xqffi.verifier.verify` → `xqffi.checker.check`, `xquad.verifier` → `xquad.checker`. The migration guide has a script for the fully qualified forms.
- **Removed CLI aliases.** `xquad asm`, `dism`, `run` and `verify` → `xquad vm asm`, `vm dis`, `vm run`, `vm check`.
- **Bounded data-flow analyses.** `xqvm::dataflow::solve(analysis, cfg)` → `solve(analysis, cfg, max_visits)`, returning `Result<_, SolveError>`.
- **New error variants.** `CheckerError` gains `AnalysisBudgetExceeded` and `JumpAcrossLoopBoundary`; `xqvm::Error` gains `NonBinaryModel`. An exhaustive match needs an arm for each.
- **Constraint opcodes need a binary model.** `ONEHOTR`, `ONEHOTC`, `EXCLUDE`, `IMPLIES`, `EQUALITY`, `ATLEAST`, `ATLEASTW` and `REDUCE` raise `NonBinaryModel` on a spin or integer model. Allocate with `BQMX`, or write coefficients with `SETLINE`, `ADDLINE`, `SETQUAD` or `ADDQUAD`. Programs compiled by `xqcp` are unaffected.

### Highlights

- The checker runs under a work budget and returns an error instead of stalling.
- Stack heights are checked in one pass over the control-flow graph, including peaks inside a block.
- `ENERGY` reads the sample in place instead of copying it.
- Python can interrupt a running VM with Ctrl-C.
- The Linux wheels are built against glibc 2.17; installing needs glibc 2.27, the NumPy floor (0.5 needed 2.34 on x86_64).

### Behaviour changes

The default checker accepts some programs 0.5 rejected and rejects some it accepted:

- Accepted now: a program whose only fault is dead code, such as a `DROP` on a dead path or a read after `HALT`.
- Rejected now: a read whose only earlier write sits after a terminator (`ReadUnsetRegister`), a stack that overflows inside one block and comes back down (`StackOverflowRisk`), and a `JUMP` or `JUMPI` into, out of or between loop bodies (`JumpAcrossLoopBoundary`).
- A program rejected by both versions can report a different error or message.

Run `xquad vm check` over stored programs to find the ones affected.

### Deprecations

The names 0.4 deprecated, apart from the CLI aliases, still work and warn in 0.6, and are removed in v0.7.0. The book's Deprecated APIs table lists each replacement.

### Packages

| Registry | Packages |
| --- | --- |
| crates.io | [xqvm](https://crates.io/crates/xqvm/0.6.0) · [xqasm](https://crates.io/crates/xqasm/0.6.0) |
| PyPI | [xquad](https://pypi.org/project/xquad/0.6.0/) |

```sh
pip install xquad==0.6.0
```

Documentation: [developers.quip.network/docs/xquad](https://developers.quip.network/docs/xquad/)

<details>
<summary>Full changelog (32 changes)</summary>

### Added

- **checker**: Reject jumps across loop bodies **[BREAKING]**
- **xquad**: Remove the deprecated top-level CLI commands **[BREAKING]**

### Changed

- **checker**: Append JumpAcrossLoopBoundary to CheckerError
- **xqvm**: Rename the bytecode verifier to a checker *

# XQuad

> **Early public release.** The instruction set, binary format, and public API
> may still change before v1.0. Production use is not recommended yet.

XQuad is a hardware-agnostic toolchain for expressing and running quadratic
optimization problems (QUBO / Ising / integer) across quantum annealers and
classical solvers. It ships as two Rust crates plus one Python distribution,
`xquad`, built around a single virtual-machine specification.

Think of it as **LLVM for quadratic models** -- a common intermediate
representation that lets you write a problem once and retarget it to any
supported backend.

- **Spec-first.** Every behaviour is nailed down in [`spec/xqvm/SPEC.md`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/spec/xqvm/SPEC.md)
  and the VM is mechanically held to it: every committed conformance vector
  runs `xqvm` in CI against the outcome the spec prescribes, and a mismatch
  fails the build.
- **Embeddable.** The Rust core supports `no_std + alloc`, so the same VM
  runs inside WASM runtimes, Substrate pallets, and native binaries.
- **Interactive.** The Python umbrella (`xquad`) is REPL and Jupyter-friendly:
  load a program once, run it with different calldata, inspect outputs by
  slot. Low-level FFI lives in `xqffi`; user-facing `Program` / `Session` /
  `RunResult` live in `xquad.program`.

## Install

### Python (from PyPI)

Install XQuad into a project environment first: a virtual environment, or a `uv` project.

```sh
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install xquad
# or, in a uv project:
uv add xquad
```

For the `xquad` command alone, outside any project, install it as a `uv` tool, with the `quip` extra for the `xquad quip` commands:

```sh
uv tool install xquad            # the xquad command
uv tool install 'xquad[quip]'    # with the xquad quip commands
```

On macOS, a user install (`pip install --user`, or pip falling back to one) puts the `xquad` command in `~/Library/Python/3.x/bin`, which is not on `PATH`; `python -m xquad` runs the same command without it.

`xquad` is the only distribution: one install carries the full pipeline, the `xquad` command, and the `xqffi`, `xqcp` and `xqsa` packages (FFI bindings, DSL, solvers), which import under their own names. Up to 0.5 those three were separate PyPI distributions; from 0.6 they ship only inside `xquad`. Prebuilt wheels are available for Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (CPython >= 3.13, glibc >= 2.27). On macOS and Windows, pip builds the `xqffi` Rust extension from source -- this requires a [Rust toolchain](https://rustup.rs/) (>= 1.85).

### GPU/QPU support

The base install includes CPU simulated annealing only. To use GPU or quantum hardware solvers, install the corresponding extra:

| Solver | Install | Prerequisite |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| NVIDIA CUDA GPU (`cuda`) | `pip install 'xquad[cuda]'` | CUDA 12.x driver + NVIDIA GPU |
| Apple Metal GPU (`metal`) | `pip install 'xquad[metal]'` | Apple Silicon Mac with a Metal device |
| D-Wave Advantage QPU (`dwave`) | `pip install 'xquad[dwave]'` | D-Wave Leap account + API token |
| Quip Network solver (`quip`) | `pip install 'xquad[quip]'` | `QUIP_RPC_URL` + a configured signer |

Extras are composable: `pip install 'xquad[cuda,dwave]'`. See [`xqsa/README.md`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/xqsa/README.md#install) for driver prerequisites and per-solver quick-starts.

For a guided walkthrough that installs XQuad, verifies it, and runs a
complete problem end to end, see
[Install XQuad](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/docs/book/src/start/README.md) in the book.

## Package map

Two Rust crates on **crates.io**:

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| [`xqvm`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xqvm) | X-Quadratic Virtual Machine interpreter, bytecode codec, opcode table (`no_std + alloc`) |
| [`xqasm`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xqasm) | `.xqasm` text-format assembler |

One Python distribution on **PyPI**, `xquad`, carrying four packages:

| Package | Description |
|---|---|
| [`xqffi`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xqffi) | PyO3 FFI bindings for `xqvm` + `xqasm` (`xqffi.vm`, `xqffi.asm`, `xqffi.checker`) |
| [`xqcp`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xqcp) | Constraint-programming DSL that compiles to `.xqasm` |
| [`xqsa`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xqsa) | Solver adapters -- CPU/GPU annealers, D-Wave QPU, Quip network |
| [`xquad`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/xquad) | Umbrella package with interactive `Program` / `Session` / `RunResult` API, and the `xquad` CLI (`xquad vm asm` / `dis` / `run` / `check`) |

The one Rust package without a crates.io artefact is the `xqffi` pyo3
crate itself -- it ships compiled inside the `xquad` wheel rather than as a
reusable Rust library.

## Quick start

### A minimal program (CLI)

```asm
; add.xqasm -- push two integers and add them
PUSH 10
PUSH 32
ADD
HALT
```

```sh
xquad vm asm add.xqasm -o add.xqb && xquad vm run add.xqb
```

### End-to-end (Python, via the umbrella)

The recommended user-facing surface is `xquad.program.Program` +
`Session` + `RunResult`. Load once, run many times with different
calldata, inspect outputs by slot:

```python
from xquad.program import Program

program = Program.from_source("""
PUSH 0
INPUT r0
PUSH 1
INPUT r1
LOAD r0
LOAD r1
ADD
STOW r2
PUSH 0
OUTPUT r2
HALT
""")

session = program.session(output_slots=1)
session.set_calldata([40, 2])
result = session.run()
assert dict(result.outputs) == {0: 42}
```

`Program.load(bytes)` takes wire-format bytecode; `Session.run()`
returns a `RunResult` with dict-keyed outputs (unset slots present as
`None`), residual stack, and step count. See
[Running Programs](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/docs/book/src/running/README.md) for the full tour.

#### Low-level / conformance surface

For conformance harnesses and one-shot execution, the raw
`xqffi.vm.Vm` is still available directly:

```python
from xqffi.asm import assemble_source
from xqffi.vm import Vm

bytecode = assemble_source(src)
v = Vm()
v.set_calldata([40, 2])
v.set_output_slots(1)
v.run(bytecode)
assert v.outputs() == [42]
```

The `xquad.vm.VM` class offers a middle tier -- a wrapper around the
Rust VM that accepts `.xqasm` source, keeps calldata, output slots and
limits across runs, and hands back the `xqffi` types unchanged.

### End-to-end worked example

[`examples/tsp/`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/tree/main/examples/tsp) shows a full Travelling Salesman Problem
driven from the `xqcp` DSL through the VM and `xqsa` solver:

```sh
uv run python examples/tsp/runner.py --seed 42
uv run python examples/maxcut/runner.py --seed 42

# Run every example and check each finds a valid solution:
make example-smoke
```

## Architecture

XQuad is a stack-based interpreter with a 256-slot register file. Registers
hold typed values -- integers, integer vectors, QUBO/Ising models
(`XqmxModel`), and candidate solutions (`XqmxSample`). A dedicated loop stack
drives `RANGE`/`ITER` iteration.

The opcode table is declared once in `xqvm/src/bytecode/types/table.rs` via
the `opcodes!` x-macro; `xqvm/opcodes.yaml` is the machine-readable
mirror, compared with the Rust macro at compile time
(`xqvm/src/bytecode/types/parity.rs`), so the two cannot drift.

The binary format (`.xqb`) opens with a fixed 15-byte XQBC header --
magic, version, calldata/output-slot counts, code length, and a CRC-32
checksum of the payload -- followed by the instruction stream: an
opcode byte followed by its operands in big-endian byte order.

See [`docs/book/src/xqvm/opcodes.md`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/docs/book/src/xqvm/opcodes.md) for
the opcode reference and
[`spec/xqvm/SPEC.md`](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/spec/xqvm/SPEC.md) for the normative spec.

## Development

### Prerequisites

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh   # stable Rust
make deps                                                          # dev tools
```

### Local setup

```sh
make xquad
```

This installs the root `xquad` project (`xqffi`, `xqcp`, `xqsa`, `xquad`)
editable into `.venv/`, builds the `xqffi` pyo3 extension via maturin,
puts the repo root on `sys.path` so scripts anywhere in the repo can
`import xqcp` / `xqsa` / `xqffi` / `xquad` naturally, and
installs the `xquad` command into `.venv/bin/`, run with `uv run xquad`.

Open a REPL with everything ready:

```sh
make repl
```

### CI-equivalent locally

```sh
make preflight    # what CI enforces, split into preflight-rs / -py / -docs / -policy
make conformance  # the specification vectors under xqvm/tests/vectors/
```

### Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow, commit
conventions, and DCO sign-off requirements. Agent guidelines for AI coding
assistants are in [AGENTS.md](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/AGENTS.md); cutting a release is documented in
[RELEASING.md](https://gitlab.com/quip.network/xquad/-/blob/main/RELEASING.md).
